summary: Turtle and rusher archetypes suffer extreme quit rates (73% and 65%) driven by round-2 difficulty spikes and a blocking bug that stalls matches at 99s. Rushers lose 69% of rounds by KO and quit 65% after round 2. Cheesers exploit a near-instant win loop (avg 16.9s round-1, 6-hit combos, zero damage taken). A single invariant violation (!stuck on BLOCK) appears on 3 turtle rounds, confirming a blocking-state bug. (Verification: 1 of 24 claims did not match the recomputed value; 2 cited seeds did not exist in the runs and were removed.)

findings.title: Turtle archetype: 73% quit rate, round-2 frustration wall, and blocking bug
findings.narrative: Turtles play long, defensive rounds (avg 76s) but 73% quit overall. Round-2 quit rate is 43% (42% after R1, 43% after R2) and win rate drops to 55% then 53%. Three turtle rounds show the invariant violation !stuck@~38-48s on BLOCK, stalling the match at the 99s cap and causing boredom/frustration quits.

seeds.why: !stuck@38.5 BLOCK causes 99s draw and boredom quit
!stuck@48.3 BLOCK, 99s draw, continues but quits after R2 boredom

findings.suggestion: Fix the BLOCK state machine so it cannot enter a stuck invariant; add a hard timeout or auto-break on block stalls. Reduce turtle round length cap from 99s to 60s to prevent boredom.

findings.suggestion: Audit cheeser move-frame data: SWEEP/JAB startup, active, recovery, and cancel windows. Add a combo-break system (pushback, damage scaling, or meter cost) so 6-hit zero-damage loops are impossible.

findings.title: Blocking invariant violation (!stuck on BLOCK) stalls matches at 99s
findings.narrative: Three turtle rounds (p0001, p0002, p0003) show the engine invariant violation '!stuck@~38-48s BLOCK', forcing the round to the 99s cap and ending in draw. This directly feeds the 73% turtle quit rate (boredom/frustration). No other archetype shows this violation.

findings.title: Round-2 global quit spike: 18% of all players quit after round 2
findings.narrative: Overall quit rate after round 2 is 18% (vs 7% after R1, 3% after R3). Turtles (43%), rushers (65%), and casuals (5%) all show elevated R2 quits. Round-2 duration drops to 41s (from 47s R1) but difficulty spikes for defensive/low-skill archetypes, causing frustration/boredom exits before round 3.

seeds.why: Turtle wins R2 87.5s but quits after R2 boredom
Rusher loses R2 23.8s KO, frustration quit
Casual wins R1 46.7s but quits after R1 frustration (early R2 quit proxy)

findings.suggestion: Smooth the round-2 difficulty curve: reduce rival damage/aggression by 10-15% in round 2, or give players a mid-session upgrade (health, meter, move unlock) before round 2 starts.
